content:
maria: Heads-up — we got another noisy batch of ECC/Xid alerts this morning in eu-west-1. Lots of single-point spikes that caused immediate node drains.

devon: saw that. alertbot fired 6 times in 2m for the same host, different cards. noisy but not persistent.

ryan: yeah telemetry shows short-lived ECC spikes right after kernel updates, then clear. probably driver jitter.

maria: current prom rule uses `increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_errors[1m]) > 0` which is too sensitive. we should aggregate by card and add a minimum sustained window + count.

sam: propose: group by (instance, gpu_index) and require `sum_over_time` or `increase` over 10m with min 3 occurrences. reduces single-sample trips.

lee: sounds reasonable. also add an explicit suppression for automated rollouts and kube-drain we trigger — otherwise we create churn.

devon: quick proof-of-concept rule I put together:
```yaml
- alert: GPU_ECC_Persistent
  expr: |
    sum by(instance, gpu_index) (increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_errors_total[10m])) >= 3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    runbook: \"eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-ecc-triage\"
```

maria: +1 on grouping. For Xid we should combine with recent `dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total` using a multi-metric check so one noisy signal doesn't trigger a drain.

ryan: multi-metric check idea: only escalate if ECC OR Xid AND (gpu_temp > 85C OR pci_errors > 0) within the same window. basically prefer correlation over single-signal.

sam: example expr: `((sum by(instance,gpu_index)(increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_errors_total[10m])) >=3) or (sum by(instance,gpu_index)(increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total[10m])) >=3)) and max_over_time(dcgm_gpu_temperature_celsius[10m]) > 85`

lee: careful using max_over_time with sparsely scraped metrics — we may get false negatives. maybe use `avg_over_time` and a low scrape interval guarantee.

devon: Ops plan:
- land rule in staging alertmanager group (eng-infra-staging)
- synthetic test: inject 3 ECC increments over 10m on a single GPU, ensure no drain until rule fires and `for:5m` passes
- test correlation scenario with elevated temp
- monitor for 48h

maria: for suppression: add a `recovery_suppression` recording rule to mark hosts in rollout windows. we have an internal label `rolling=true` on nodes undergoing driver-upgrade job. use `unless on(instance) rolling == 1` to suppress during maintenance windows.

ops-bot: Alert: node gpu-node-34.eu-west-1 triggered dcgm-exporter:ECC-spike (3 events) at 2024-11-02T08:12:09Z

ryan: noted — gpu-node-34 is on a driver kubejob this morning. explains it.

sam: question: if we relax sensitivity, are we ok accepting a slightly longer time to detect real failures? tradeoff between N minutes of degraded performance vs frequent drains.

maria: yes, we prefer fewer false drains. we should add autoscaling buffer and a temporary cluster-level overprovision of 10% while tuning. operations cost small compared to churn.

devon: I'll open a PR with: new promrule (staging), alertmanager silence logic for `rolling`, and a unit test harness for synthetic ECC/Xid injection.

sam: add a dashboard widget that shows `alerts by gpu_index` and a rolling histogram of event durations. helps tune windows.

lee: reminder: update oncall runbook — change recommended immediate-drain threshold to persistent cross-metric for 15m.

maria: timeline: devon PR today, staging deploy tomorrow, 48h watch, then gradual prod roll (canary 10% nodes) if green.

devon: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4981 : Includes rule, tests, and alertmanager tweak. PTAL. :eyes:

sam: lgtm from me. I'll help run the synthetic tests after staging deploy.

ryan: I'll coordinate with driver-upgrades to mark nodes as `rolling=1` so we don't get noise.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees repeated drains overnight ping me directly.
